summary: Persistent 5xx pulses during tenant concurrency surge caused by runtime file descriptor exhaustion
description:
Issue summary: Customer reported repeated short-lived waves of 5xx (502/503) affecting streaming and short-poll generation routes for a single dedicated tenant. Impact: Several production endpoints returned 502/503 intermittently for ~10-30s pulses, causing dropped streams and failed request retries; observed by Nimbus Health as increased error rate and user-visible failures. Environment: Dedicated pool for customer in us-east-1; mixed embedding/chat traffic; model pinned to redwood/gptx-3.2. Initial symptom window: 2026-03-10 01:12–03:40 UTC.

Steps to reproduce: not reliably reproducible from a single synthetic test; reproduces under sustained concurrent tenant traffic + aggressive background prefetch for large prompt sets. Support template fields below contain logs, metrics, and timeline.
steps_to_reproduce: Send mixed streaming and non-streaming requests at 150 concurrent connections from single tenant with varied prompt lengths (200–400 tokens).
Trigger background model prefetch by submitting a large-batch evaluation job (customer internal test) to the tenant simultaneously.
Observe intermittent 502/503 on streaming sessions and short-lived elevated 5xx pulses in API gateway and runtime metrics.
logs: 2026-03-10T01:15:04Z runtime[pid=1843]: OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files
2026-03-10T01:15:04Z runtime[pid=1843]: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/opt/serving/prefetch/worker.py", line 412, in _open_prefetch_stream
2026-03-10T01:15:04Z apigw[edge-id=apigw-12]: upstream read error: EOF (502) for route /v1/chat/stream
metrics_observed: API gateway 5xx rate for tenant spiked from baseline 0.2% to 8.6% in 30s windows
Runtime open file descriptor count on host node climbed from ~2k to >65k before failures
Accept queue drop rate increased concurrently with runtime 'watchdog restart' events
Concurrent streaming sessions for tenant reached sustained 180+ connections (above expected 120 cap)
investigation_notes: Initial triage (support): Correlated apigw 502s to upstream runtime restarts and EMFILE in runtime logs. Tenant traffic patterns show high short-lived stream connects plus a background evaluation triggering prefetch activity.
SRE ran live diagnostics on affected runtime host: lsof snapshot showed thousands of TCP sockets and many /tmp/prefetch/*.tmp file handles left open by prefetch worker processes.

Hypothesis: Prefetch worker has a filehandle leak when prefetching large prompt embeddings; under high concurrency the leak climbs until process cannot open sockets/files, watchdog restarts the worker and upstream returns 502/503.

Temporary mitigation: increased ulimit -n for affected pods to 100k and disabled aggressive prefetch for the tenant via per-tenant config (rollback to conservative prefetch window). This immediately reduced recurrence of pulses.

Root cause identified by runtime eng: missing close() paths in prefetch worker error-handling when partial reads fail; also prefetch created temp files that were not removed on cancellation. See PRs referenced.

2026-03-10 02:22 UTC — SRE (Marta Delgado): Confirmed EMFILE traces on node runtime-ue1-34. Collecting lsof + pmap. Noted many /tmp/prefetch files. Temporarily bumped ulimit and paused tenant prefetch config.

2026-03-10 03:00 UTC — Liam O'Connor (Runtime Eng): Deployed emergency patch to dev cluster to ensure prefetch filehandles are closed on error; tests pass. Preparing cut for prod. Also queued PR to add FD growth alerting.

2026-03-12 09:00 UTC — Liam O'Connor (Runtime Eng): Hotfix merged and rolled out to affected dedicated pool. Follow-up task INT-2409 created to harden prefetch and add chaos tests for FD leaks. Marking support ticket resolved and informing customer of permanent fix.
resolution: Hotfix applied: fixed missing close() paths in prefetch worker and added cleanup for temporary files. Emergency mitigation (increased ulimit, disabled aggressive prefetch for tenant) limited recurrence during rollout. Hotfix deployed to prod dedicated pool on 2026-03-11; metrics show 5xx back to baseline. Postmortem and follow-up tasks created (INT-2409) to add FD-growth alerting and integration tests. Customer notified and verified.
next_steps: INT-2409: Add unit/chaos tests to prefetch path to catch FD leaks
Add an FD-growth alert (pager at Sev1) for runtime hosts tied to tenant pools
Document prefetch configuration knobs and safe defaults in runbook
Schedule capacity review for tenant to discuss connection caps and prefetch behavior
